findings.passage: “Missouri should have the strongest election laws in the country,” Sen. Brattin said. “There were enough problems around the country in the 2020 election that we need to do everything in our power to make sure ballots and voting are secure and that voters have full confidence in our elections.”
findings.note: Senate press release in his name on the Senate passing HB 1878, which the release says covers voter ID, a ban on private funding of election offices, and a ban on drop boxes and mail-in voting.

findings.passage: “There is no issue more pressing to our country than the integrity of our elections,” Sen. Brattin said. “If we don’t have confidence and trust in our elections, than we don’t have a country. Free and fair elections are part of what has allowed our country to endure and thrive for almost 250 years, and we owe it to the voters, our state and our country to fight for election integrity.”
findings.note: Same release; he says election integrity is the most pressing issue.

findings.passage: “It’s a part of being a functioning member of society to apply for benefits from the government. So, if we have a process that requires that, we’ll pay for it, how is this a detrimental thing other than we’re helping them provide that documentation, but also at the same time ensuring a safe, secure election?” asked Brattin.
findings.note: Quoted by Missourinet in a story on another senator's bill requiring proof of citizenship to register; he says the state would pay to help people get the documents.
